answer: Proof of space: each earning identity must fill 2 TB of disk with data derived from its own key, so one plot cannot serve two keys. Every epoch validators pick random sectors and demand the matching bytes within seconds, which only works if the plot is really stored. Ten fakes need 20 TB, a cost that splitting one disk cannot dodge. A gale of cheap new drives can still buy in, so this prices identities rather than proving persons; when disk prices hit a nadir, the plot size must rise. A plot is not crystal-clear proof of honesty, only of storage.
